result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give distinct, practical layouts for all four formats, a horizontal banner, a clear list of what gets dropped, and safe-zone guidance. B is stronger because it flags that 14 November 2026 is a Saturday, not a Friday, which is a real error to fix before printing. It also adds useful checks: whether the post reads at thumbnail size, and whether the event page already shows the title above the banner. A is equally thorough on layout and a little more explicit about dropping the address, but it misses the date problem. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers meet the rubric well: each keeps a consistent hierarchy, lays the banner out side by side, says what is dropped in each format, and handles the story safe zones (B also covers poster viewing distance). A wins because it catches that 14 November 2026 is a Saturday, so the stated Friday is wrong for this year, which would prevent a printing error. A's layouts are also slightly more distinct from one another, while B's poster and story are close to the same stack.
